Alex P.: Heads up — I'm proposing we consolidate the various route_profile lookup paths into a single route_profile_index_v2. The motivation: console queries that assemble route cards are hitting 3 different joins and slow down dashboards. Thinking of a phased roll (shadow-write -> read-probe -> gradual traffic cutover). Thoughts?
Maya R.: :eyes: Sounds promising. Any schema changes required or just a new index/table?
Alex P.: New table + index. We'll populate with a pre-computed score (quota_score) and a last_seen_at for quicker UI sorting. Minimal columns, mostly denormalized material per-route to avoid repeated joins.
Sam K.: Can we avoid changing the ingest path? If we add a new materialized table we could drive it from a streaming job (rehydration pipeline) and keep the source contract untouched.
Irene L.: Streaming job + shadow-write from current writer for parity would be safest. Then a read adapter that prefers v2 when available.
Jordan S.: Agree on read adapter. We should also consider stale vs fresh semantics in the console: when v2 row exists but timestamp older than X, fallback to canonical joins.
Maya R.: Good point — define a staleness window. Maybe 10m for live dashboards, 24h for long-tail reports?
Alex P.: Proposed cutover plan in bullets: shadow-write for 48h, run read-probe against 5% of console queries, measure discrepancies, widen to 25% then 100%. Rollback path is to disable read adapter and keep v2 being written (so no lost data).
Sam K.: What's the expected population time for the initial hydrate? Our route universe is ~120M route_ids. If hydrating at 200k/s that's ~10 minutes? wait math off...
Irene L.: 120M / 200k/s = 600s -> ~10 minutes, yes. But we need to account for upstream rate limits and windowing, plus idempotency checks. Realistic start might be 1.5-2x that.
Alex P.: Good catch — plan assumes 5-20 min hydration depending on parallelism. We'll stage the bulk seed with a fast export/import job and let streaming reconcile deltas.
Jordan S.: SQL checks we should run during probe: \n```sql\n-- count mismatches where UI-sort differs\nSELECT count(1) FROM route_profile_index_v2 v2\nJOIN route_profiles rp ON rp.route_id = v2.route_id\nWHERE v2.quota_score != rp.computed_quota_score;\n```\nAlso compare top-k for a sample tenant to validate ordering.
Maya R.: Metrics to watch during canary: console p99 query latency, console 5xx rate, v2 write error rate, streaming lag (ms), and hydrate backfill throughput.
Sam K.: Add memory/CPU on the ingestion writer host to that list. The new index writes could increase IOPS.
Irene L.: For safety gate, let's add an automated anomaly detector: if probe mismatch rate > 0.1% OR console p99 increases by >15% for 5m, auto-disable read-probe and notify #incidents.
Alex P.: Deploy bot will run the migration job id then post status. plan to run migration job in night window but do canary during business hours for visibility.
deploy-bot: migration job route-profile-index-v2 started by @AlexP (job_id=rpv2-20260321-01), snapshot phase=seed-export, progress=0%
Maya R.: What about queries that rely on joins across route_metadata that aren't represented in v2? We'll need a quick fallback path in the read adapter for those fields.
Alex P.: Yes read adapter will be field-aware. If a requested field isn't present in v2, it'll fall back to the join path. That keeps feature parity during rollout.
Jordan S.: Can we avoid touching RPC contracts? I'm nervous about breaking internal SDKs that ask for route_profiles.
Irene L.: No contract changes — adapter is internal to console service. SDKs remain unchanged.
Sam K.: One more: retention. v2 will be compacted monthly. Older route snapshots should be archived to cold storage. Need a small TTL policy and compaction job.
Alex P.: Noted. Final checklist before we start shadow-write: 1) seed export job + idempotent importer 2) streaming bridge for deltas 3) read adapter + staleness rule 4) monitoring dashboards (mismatch rate, p99, errors) 5) automated safety gate 6) rollback doc and SQL (delete triggers off, disable adapter).
Maya R.: :thumbsup: Add me as oncall for first 24h of canary.
Irene L.: I'll own the streaming bridge and tests for idempotency.
Sam K.: I'll add the performance dashboards and an explain-plan watcher for the console queries that switch to v2.
Jordan S.: I'll draft the rollback commands and the runbook entries.
Alex P.: Great — I'll spin up the seed job and post the job id here. Plan target: start shadow-write tomorrow 0200 UTC, canary start 1000 UTC. If anything looks off we'll hit the safety gate. :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: migration job rpv2-20260321-01 progress=seed-export: 100% -> queued for import (operator=@AlexP)
